The Committee goes on to argue that the Interim Report represents a complete departure from the relevant precedent factors, which have been established in prior Commission decisions. Those decisions have consistently held that the commercial zone and terminal area exemptions apply only to the "local" and "intracommunity" movement of traffic as opposed to intercity or intercommunity operations. The findings of the Interim Report falter because the Commission has failed to demonstrate that the areas to be included within the expanded commercial zones and terminal areas are "unified" or share a "cohesive community interest" with base municipalities so as to form "distinct communities".
The Committee asserts that since the Interim Report is bereft of reliance on precedent to support zone expansion, the Commission has chosen to rely exclusively on reasons relating to demography and industrial location patterns. It is the Committee's position that two Commission policies severely discount the importance of considerations of demography and industrial relocation.
